claim: The Data Layer defines three distinct extension-point interface pairs: PollingDataSource+Extractor, NotificationSource+NotificationExtractor, and EndpointSource+EndpointExtractor -- these are the exact Go interfaces a custom, non-Kubernetes backend implementation would need to satisfy.
stance_target: enumerating the concrete plugin interfaces for data sources/collectors, per the research focus
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Data Layer design page
quoted_support: The Data Layer is built around three primary source types, each paired with a corresponding extractor interface

claim: Only the NotificationSource interface (concretely k8s-notification-source) is intrinsically Kubernetes-coupled -- it binds to the controller-runtime manager and watches a specific Kubernetes GVK (CRD or core API object); PollingDataSource (metrics-data-source) and EndpointSource (endpoint-notification-source) are backend-agnostic by construction, operating on whatever Endpoint objects already exist in the EPP's datastore.
stance_target: precisely isolating which Data Layer interface carries the Kubernetes/pod assumption versus which do not
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Data Layer design page
quoted_support: k8s-notification-source ... can be configured to watch a single Kubernetes GVK (either a CRD or a k8s core API) and dispatches NotificationEvents to registered NotificationExtractors when objects are created, updated, or deleted.

claim: As of this documentation snapshot, there are no upstream Extractors that consume the NotificationSource interface at all -- meaning the one interface that IS Kubernetes-bound (k8s-notification-source) is not currently load-bearing for any shipped scoring/filtering functionality, only theoretically available.
stance_target: practical scope of what actually needs replacing versus what is dormant/unused for a non-k8s backend
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Data Layer design page, as of Sep 2026 snapshot
quoted_support: There are currently no upstream extractors that require this source.

claim: The runtime starts one Collector per endpoint for PollingDataSource plugins, which polls the source at a configured interval and passes results to associated Extractors -- confirming per-endpoint polling is the primary mechanism for metrics pulling, independent of how the endpoint's address was discovered.
stance_target: mechanics of the metrics-polling extension point relevant to reusing it for non-pod endpoints
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Data Layer design page
quoted_support: The runtime starts a Collector for every new endpoint. The collector polls the source at a configured interval and passes the result to associated extractors.

claim: Endpoint Attributes are stored in a thread-safe, type-safe map on each Endpoint object and are the primary channel by which the Data Layer shares information with the rest of the EPP (scheduling, flow control) -- this Endpoint/Attribute abstraction, not the Kubernetes Pod type, is the actual unit the scheduler and scorers operate on.
stance_target: identifying the EPP's internal data model as already Pod-agnostic at the scheduling-plugin boundary
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Data Layer design page
quoted_support: Endpoint Attributes: A thread-safe, type-safe map stored on each Endpoint. Attributes are the primary way information is shared between the Data Layer and other EPP components.
